shipped_rows.title_o: Ignoring History, Denying Racism: Mounting Evidence for the Marley Hypothesis and Epistemologies of Ignorance

blind_target.authors: Nelson, J. C., Adams, G., & Salter, P. S.
blind_target.title: The Marley Hypothesis: Denial of racism reflects ignorance of history.
blind_target.evidence_quote: In the 2 studies reported herein, we attempted to replicate prior research on the Marley Hypothesis, which argues that White Americans are more ignorant of historical instances of racism than Black Americans and that this ignorance of history mediates racial differences in perceptions of racism (Bonam et al., 2018, Study 1; Nelson et al., 2013).
blind_target.outcome_quote: Contrary to our predictions, Study 1 failed to replicate results of prior studies on the Marley Hypothesis.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly judge both replication studies failures of the central Marley mediation hypothesis; replicated ancillary findings do not alter this overall verdict.

luna_triage.reason: The paper explicitly re-tests the Marley Hypothesis and directly names Nelson et al. (2013) as one of the two prior studies it attempts to replicate. The supplied shipped row 2085 is Bonam et al. (2018), Study 1, a distinct original paper; it does not represent Nelson et al. (2013). The source reports the replication comparison in its Results and its identity in the abstract/introduction.
luna_triage.omission_quote: Thus, the present research failed to replicate the mediation effect found in prior studies.
luna_triage.identity_quote: Two provocative studies on the Marley Hypothesis suggest that White Americans are more ignorant of historical instances of racism than Black Americans and that ignorance of history mediates racial differences in perceptions of racism (Nelson, Adams, & Salter, 2013; Bonam, Das, Coleman, & Salter, 2018).
